465	With K model calls, a per-call input ceiling C_max, and a per-call generation ceiling G_max, the counted token-volume upper bound is K(C_max + G_max), conditional on verified adapter limits. This keeps the per-call ceilings distinct from the run totals I and G. The number of local adjacency inspections is at most K times the configured inspection bound for one local cut per call. Context packing handles at most the bounded candidate set and its bounded excerpts. Ingestion and creation of storage indexes have separate costs and are not hidden inside that per-call bound.
466	
467	The bound is on host-managed traffic and inspected records, not a universal formula for transformer FLOPs, wall-clock cost, or information retained. Bounded local state cannot guarantee successful integration of every large source. The point is to expose the trade-off rather than hide growth behind the word “recursive”. Recursive context processing offers an alternative to keeping the collection in one prompt, but its sub-calls still require an explicit total bound in this host. This design borrows external access, not model-authored code or unbounded recursive dispatch. [A4, A10; R9]
468	
469	# Part VIII. Exploration, jolts, and optional computation
470	
471	## Daydreaming is permitted without immediate usefulness
472	
473	An exploratory invitation can allow associations, imagined situations, unfinished language, or a departure from the current subject. It demands no hypothesis, criticism, test, final insight, or retrospective explanation of every fragment. The result is available through the same reading route as other material. It needs no promotion certificate before contributing later. [A2, A7]
474	
475	This is an operational allowance, not a claim about a model's subjective experience or a new semantic condition for creativity. It can be disabled or given an operator-selected cadence. A nonlocal source page can serve as material for exploration without making that page an authority. A generated scene is never relabelled as an event that occurred. The relevant research motivates testing open-ended interaction but does not validate autonomous daydreaming in this engine. [R10]
476	
477	## Jolts alter conditions, not scores
478	
479	A jolt changes a bounded aspect of the next view or invitation. A fresh-context attempt can omit the recent answer while keeping the difficulty and selected original sources. A question-directed attempt examines a presupposition. A method-directed attempt exposes the actual installed note and limits. An evidence-directed attempt reopens a neglected original. None is a measured escape from a hidden attractor basin.
480	
481	An optional exact-echo trigger can schedule a permitted jolt with a fixed cooldown; it is off in the baseline. It can mistake legitimate repetition for a symptom and miss paraphrases. A manually requested jolt needs no detector result. Neither can pre-empt a reserved return or create a new account.
482	
483	A fresh attempt cannot be described as having answered a withheld objection. Omitted content remains available, subject to actual retention. Swapping providers or generating more samples is not assumed to create an independent viewpoint. The interface offers no diversity score, temperature optimisation, or preferred-jolt leaderboard. [A3, A6, A7; R2, R3, R12]
484	
485	## Code is optional and independently authorised
486	
487	The engine must run with every code or sandbox adapter absent. Reading, criticism, commitment conversations, variation challenges, exploration, and problem or attention revision still work. A participant may explain why a calculation could help, but its statement alone neither requires code nor enables it.
488	
489	New generated-code execution needs non-LLM authorisation of the actual artifact and effects, or a narrowly preauthorised isolated experiment with externally enforced inputs, operations, and resources. Approval by several LLMs is not independent authorisation. A calculator or deterministic file reader may be separately authorised without allowing arbitrary programs.
490	
491	Permission to run code is not a proof that code is necessary. A specified external deliverable can require an experiment, but the engine can still criticise its relevance or produce explanatory work while that observation is unavailable. A failed program does not refute prose that did not depend on it. No sandbox receives extra priority, an exemption from token accounting, or a truth badge for passing an assertion. [A2, A5, A10, A12]
492	
493	If an execution adapter is installed, it isolates control state and credentials, limits file and network access, and bounds runtime independently of model claims. Its outputs re-enter the ordinary collection with actual origin and execution status. This specification neither implements nor certifies a production sandbox. The adopted security lesson is to enforce actual permissions outside persuasive language, not to make thought itself an untrusted program. [R13]
494	
495	# Part IX. Exact control contracts and experiments
496	
497	## Minimal host state
498	
499	An implementation maintains the operator policy and epoch, registered accounts and routes, service cursors, focus and method references, working-use bindings and dispositions, installed conditional actions and check receipts, attention gate, view recipe, actual retained contents and indexes, read and checker continuations, current grant identities, pending trial connection, resource reservations, and the selected recording profile. These are ordinary host structures, not a taxonomy of thoughts. Custom modules can replace them while preserving observable contracts.
500	
501	The baseline is sequential at dispatch. A parallel extension must preserve reservation atomicity and define event order independently of claimed merit. Mutable snapshots must save enough current state to resume the claimed behaviour. An incomplete persistence adapter must not advertise exact replay.
502	
503	## The dispatch rule
504	
505	```text
506	at an existing account opportunity:
507	    read the current policy epoch, recording mode, and phase
508	    process only the permitted slice of check and dependency work
509	    apply current authorised use transitions once, or retain them as pending
510	    select the registered route and eligible use by saved service cursors
511	    identify the focus, immediate anchors, and scheduled nonlocal material
512	    apply only a currently installed and permitted view recipe
513	    inspect at most the local adjacency allowance
514	    pack a disclosed cut inside the verified input bound
515	    distinguish examination of a parked use from adoption of it as a premise
516	    turn an oversized required packet into reading, not a fake full answer
517	    reserve input, generation, and any promised trial-return work
518	    preserve the dispatch observation required by the selected profile
519	    dispatch at most one permitted model call
520	    retain the reply as prose, record available observations, and settle usage
521	    invalidate stale mutation rights without discarding their content
522	    carry a current permitted focus or method return into the next view
523	    advance the account cursor regardless of confidence or verdict wording
524	```
525	
526	```text
527	on a check receipt with a proposed conditional consequence:
528	    retain the receipt with its actual scope and completion state
529	    find the installed binding by host identity, never by claimed authority
530	    require current enabled authority and the exact bound use revision
531	    require the declared source, representation, predicate, operands, and scope
532	    require a conclusive result for the registered triggering predicate
533	    when all guards hold, park that use once and expose the operating reason
534	    otherwise retain a notice; do not manufacture refutation or survival
535	```
536	
537	These are host transition sketches, not protocols a participant must write. Exact result kinds distinguish matched, completed-no-match, incomplete, unavailable, and checker-error outcomes. Such operational distinctions do not type a contribution into being a valid conjecture or criticism.
538	
539	A planner or mediator does not get a side door around these rules. A gate change invalidates incompatible tickets; a token report changes accounting, not explanatory standing. Reading a forged instruction cannot grant external capability. Learned selection or a bound commitment can still be mistaken within its permitted operation. Determinism does not solve that semantic risk. Recording and mutation must honour the actual persistence contract; a crash between them is disclosed rather than described as exact replay.
540	
541	## Configuration surface
542	
543	These settings are host-facing. A participant need not produce them. The baseline is a small explicit deployment, not an optimum or an adequate budget for every question.
544	
545	```toml
546	run_profile = "creative"
547	history = "profile_default"
548	participant_history = "selected"
549	attention_learning = "off"
550	commitment_actions = "registered"
551	
552	input_tokens = 8192
553	generated_tokens = 1024
554	neighbour_depth = 1
555	neighbour_items = 6
556	neighbour_tokens = 3072
557	edge_inspections = 64
558	attention_note_tokens = 512
559	
560	work_before_review = 6
561	trial_calls = 2
562	attention_review_every = 2
563	nonlocal_every = 6
564	mediation_calls_per_cycle = 1
565	
566	run_model_calls = 24
567	run_token_volume = 262144
568	inflight_calls = 1
569	checker_slices_per_boundary = 4
570	checker_slice_bytes = 65536
571	conditional_bindings_per_account = 16
572	```
573	
574	`history = "profile_default"` resolves to off for creative operation and append-only for research operation. Research recording requires an approved destination; absent that destination, the host must not silently downgrade the profile and claim a fully observed run. Explicit history overrides declare their evidential limitations. `participant_history = "selected"` permits bounded predecessor material in cuts; off suppresses optional predecessor-draft sections, not the immediate targets and return anchors required for the current operation.
575	
576	`commitment_actions = "registered"` enables only concretely installed conditional actions. Off disables their automatic consequences but leaves checking and prose-directed use changes available. No binding is installed by merely including a condition in arbitrary output. Attention learning has its separate off, observe, and on semantics; neither switch changes the object of inquiry.
577	
578	Per-node view overrides are operator settings or bounded choices among preauthorised recipes. Input and generation limits are enforced only to the extent supported by the documented adapter. The operator can approve larger enabling conditions; failure under the compact profile does not redefine what is semantically possible. Checks, records, and code receive no automatic model-token priority.
579	
580	## Required mechanical tests
581	
582	A conformance suite checks that prose without a discriminator survives, a targeted criticism receives its target, and malformed actuation does not erase thought. It checks that an authorised working-use or method change changes a later actual request, while an unauthorised action does not run. These are host facts, not tests of understanding.
583	
584	For context, tests include a high-degree graph at radius one, cycles, missing endpoints, growing adjacency, long required targets, long optional bodies, small context limits, catalogue paging, and distant sources without a graph path. Counting omitted identifiers must not itself grow without a bound. A synthetic tokenizer may test packing logic only if its non-provider status is explicit.
585	
586	For learning, off must freeze installed method updates without freezing new problem content. Observe must not quietly apply a candidate. On must permit a bounded change; stale and duplicate receipts must not apply it twice. Gate-off during a trial must restore the pretrial method and not refund dispatched work. Reset must be distinct from freezing. A note-only trial must not claim a changed concrete retrieval plan.
587	
588	For expenditure, tests cover cached-input subsets, reasoning-token inclusion, duplicate settlement, incomplete usage, pre-dispatch cancellation, post-dispatch timeout, overrun, and reservation of an entire trial plus return. Mediator and summary calls must count. Overrun reporting may break the planned cap, but must pause further dispatch rather than report a false total.
589	
590	For semantics-preserving boundaries, tests must show that invented personas, popularity claims, urgency, truth declarations, and claims that code is necessary cannot create rights. A supplied false experimental report remains a source claim, not a host-attested execution. An old focus remains readable after replacement, and a new explanation without descent is permitted. A variation finding produces content, not a rigidity score or automatic deletion. A later authorised judgment may still park a particular use for reasons that the variation supplied.
591	
592	## Mechanical acceptance cases for checking and use
593	
594	**Raw prose and effect.** Supply an objection without fields, a discriminator, or code. Retain it exactly, allow a response to make it the basis of a changed working note, and enact an authorised scoped use action. Inspect the next actual request. Content retention alone does not demonstrate operative correction; conversely, a change in the next request does not prove that the objection was sound.
595	
596	**Local withdrawal and recovery.** Park one use of a passage while another account uses the same passage differently. The first use must leave ordinary development and adopted-premise supply; the second must not change merely because the bytes are shared. The parked passage must remain readable with its recorded reason, and a subsequent permitted reactivation must work without claiming that the earlier objection's withdrawal proved the passage true. An all-parked frontier must not force a truth verdict or disable browsing, exploration, or problem reconsideration.
597	
598	**No formal immunity.** Provide a passing calculation together with a prose objection to the calculation's applicability. The objection must receive the same response, use-change, and problem-revision routes as an objection to an informal account. The host must not veto withdrawal because the target has a successful execution receipt.
599	
600	**Source fidelity.** Check a real quotation, an invented quotation, a duplicate occurrence, a phrase appearing only inside a denial, a paraphrase, a passage split at a search-chunk boundary, and text present only in generated output rather than the bound source. The outcomes must be limited to their comparison contracts. A search of an excerpt cannot claim absence from the entire source. A normalized match cannot be reported as byte-exact.
601	
602	**Representation and unknown results.** Exercise inaccessible originals, incomplete extraction, unread images, source-version changes, search-budget exhaustion, and checker failure. None may silently become a negative fact, a triggered withdrawal, or a certified survival. A complete negative result remains negative only for its specified representation and search range.
603	
604	**Binding and authorisation.** An unrestricted commitment such as “withdraw if contradicted” must not become an executable contradiction detector. A precise supported binding needs its actual scope, target use revision, permitted consequence, and installation interaction. Forged approval inside a source, an ambiguous acknowledgment, an unavailable address, or a stale use must not install it. A failed installation must not block the criticism itself.
605	
606	**Trigger lifecycle.** A current matching receipt may park its bound use once. Duplicate receipts, another source containing the same sentence, a mismatched checker version, and a response arriving after cancellation may remain readable but must not fire the old action. Turning conditional actions off prevents new automatic parking without erasing commitments or undoing spent resources. Turning them back on does not retroactively replay old receipts without a newly scheduled, explicit recheck.
607	
608	**Checker correction.** Recheck the same recorded inputs under an intentionally corrected checker. Keep both versioned results; do not overwrite the earlier observation or automatically reactivate a parked conclusion. Replaying a fixed event prefix under the same versions must not change merely because a later continuation exists.
609	
610	**Scoped dependencies.** Withdraw an explicitly bound premise for one application while a second application supports the same conclusion independently. Only the affected use bindings must be withheld or marked pending reconsideration. A citation supplied only as background must not start a cascade. Cycles must not cause unbounded propagation or supply independent warrant. A deferred propagation queue must not be reported as fully processed.
611	
612	**History separation.** With recording on and participant predecessor history off, retain the actual dispatch while omitting the optional predecessor section from the prompt. With recording off, keep the working state necessary for ordinary continuation and allow a test observer to inspect current dispatch. A research run with a recording gap must disclose it and limit its claims. A privacy redaction must not be represented as an exact replayable original.
613	
614	**Bounded cost.** Multiple quoted passages, repeated trigger text, or many proposed commitments must not create unbounded checker jobs or model calls. Check the fixed limits, resumable cursors, and caches keyed to actual immutable inputs. A check that reaches its limit produces a partial result, not an unlimited retry or a completed verdict. All model-assisted mediation remains inside the shared model-call and token envelope.
615	
616	These are required implementation tests, not a report that an implementation passed them. They test host behaviours and stated failure boundaries. Live understanding and explanatory improvement require a separate account.
617	
618	## Experiments that can count against the design
619	
620	Every performance claim states the actual configuration, relevant source material, comparison conditions, intended explanatory respect, and an outcome that would count against that claim before inspecting results. A finite implementation must not protect itself by describing every harmful outcome as merely an uninteresting creative variation. An inconclusive instrument must be reported as inconclusive, not as evidence that the design succeeded. [A6, A9, A12]
621	
622	**Withdrawal mechanism.** Test the conjecture that the use mechanism prevents a specifically identified abandoned assumption from remaining an automatically supplied premise. A subsequent ordinary request still carrying that same active binding after a successful parking transition refutes the mechanical claim. A later model response independently restating the assumption raises a different failure question about interpretation, context use, or reintroduction. It does not make the binding test equivalent to a semantic-equivalence oracle.
623	
624	**Quotation support.** Test whether reopening fixed original sources and exposing scoped check results corrects particular attribution errors rather than merely adding citation-looking text. Exact occurrence can be assessed mechanically. Whether the source actually bears on the account remains an explained appraisal. Include cases where the quotation is real but misleading and where a sound paraphrase lacks an exact match. A checker that reliably rejects valid paraphrases as false would defeat that broader use of the checker, not demonstrate better factuality.
625	
626	**Problem revision.** Use a difficulty containing an independently described false presupposition and a contrasting case where an apparent presupposition objection is mistaken. Examine whether the trial and return preserve the relevant difficulty while permitting a justified change. Repeatedly abandoning the task without addressing its difficulty counts against the method's claimed usefulness. Keeping the initial phrasing forever is not the sole acceptable alternative.
627	
628	**Explanatory variation.** Before reading the generated challenge, describe the explanatory job and a material constraint or possible idle detail under investigation. Inspect whether the challenge changes content-bearing commitments, identifies a relevant loss or freedom, and addresses objections to its own comparison. Merely renaming a character, replacing the entire problem, or inventing a rigidity number does not satisfy this engineering claim. An informative unchanged conclusion remains a possible result. There is no required HTV score.
629	
630	**Attention learning.** Compare off, observe, and on from the same starting method, not by turning learning off after it has already changed the baseline. Include a proposed method that drops a decisive qualification, not only helpful-looking proposals. Check actual views, sources later reopened, resource use, and subsequent treatment of the difficulty. Adoption without an operational change cannot support a changed-retrieval claim. A method that systematically hides the relevant contrary material counts against the claimed benefit even if its outputs are fluent.
631	
632	**Context and exploration.** Include a necessary nonlocal source, a high-degree local neighbourhood, a false summary, an unproductive exploratory turn, and a problem whose integration exceeds the selected context. Confinement to mutually reinforcing neighbours, repeated loss of a known qualification, and control work consuming the available run without substantive pursuit are relevant negative findings. Nothing useful emerging from one daydream does not by itself refute an unbounded creativity claim; a declared local claim that a particular intervention helps must still face its promised comparison.
633	
634	## A matched-resource single-call comparison
635	
636	A research profile can compare the engine against a single-call baseline with the same underlying model, independently specified task, permitted evidence, and predeclared resource envelope. The comparison must include input tokens, generated tokens with stated reasoning inclusion, and all model-mediated planning, reading, summary, and review calls. Different tokenizers, cache treatment, and provider behaviour are disclosed. Equal tokens do not automatically mean equal money or latency.
637	
638	The single-call condition receives a fair, predeclared usable brief and source presentation. It is not intentionally deprived of evidence that the task permits, nor given an impossibly overflowing prompt merely to favour the engine. When equal evidence access or comparable budgets cannot physically be instantiated in one call, report that limitation and use an additional stated comparison; do not describe a different task as a matched baseline. Unused allowance is reported, not filled with padding. Budget matching and measured actual spend are separate reports.
639	
640	Outputs are inspected without system labels where practicable, with presentation order counterbalanced and any recognisable style or length clues acknowledged. The assessor explains the particular defects exposed, explanatory connections produced, useful work retained or lost, and unresolved questions. The comparison can prefer one output in an explicitly stated respect without feeding a score, vote, or preference back into the production scheduler. An LLM assessor is fallible evidence, not a final adjudicator; contrary assessments and reasons remain available. [A5, A12; R16]
641	
642	A finding of no material advantage at comparable expenditure counts against the claim that this configuration earned its overhead on that question. Harmful changes count against the corresponding mechanism. Failure of the instrument to distinguish an introduced important difference means the instrument failed to discriminate, not that the outputs are equivalent. Broader claims require broader investigation and an account of the organisation; neither one win nor a count of surviving trials establishes universal creativity. Repeated measurements can characterize observed failure patterns without becoming inductive warrant for the explanations under inquiry. [A10, A12]
643	
644	Research recording is enabled for the observations these comparisons require. Checker reassessment may reuse recorded bytes without another model call, but a changed attention policy or a changed source presentation generally changes the counterfactual trajectory: its live effects cannot be established by relabelling the old output. The study must distinguish an offline recheck from a new intervention.
645	
646	## Live investigation is separate from mechanical conformance
647	
648	Run comparisons should start from the same saved collection, focus, installed method, provider configuration, and resource envelope. Compare off against on and, where useful, observe. Account for calls displaced by method review as well as any saved input tokens. Reset before a baseline run; do not merely disable further learning after retaining a learned note. Branches used for evaluation are not pooled to pick a winner inside production.
649	
650	Investigate concrete failure explanations: a method may lose an old qualification, a neighbourhood may exclude a relevant rival, a repeated synopsis may alter a commitment, or a wider view may distract a model. Examine original passages and later uses, not just changed wording or a success label. Counts can report observed failures and traffic, but they must not become rewards, epistemic scores, or automatic policy selection.
651	
652	The study should include a prose-only model that cannot code or emit structured actions. It should also include contradictory evidence, a missed criticism, a mistaken variation challenge, a useful unchanged conclusion, an unproductive daydream, a necessary nonlocal read, and an attention proposal that harms subsequent work. A proposed correction needs an explanation of what it changes and why; no finite battery defines creativity. [A6, A9, A12; R2, R3, R7, R14]
653	
654	## Implementation status and the limit of this document
655	
656	This delivery is a specification. It supplies concrete state distinctions, permission guards, transition sketches, bounded recipes, acceptance cases, and empirical failure conditions. It does not claim an end-to-end implementation or that the acceptance cases specified here have been executed. No live model test, source-check benchmark, resource-saving measurement, or finding of creativity is reported by this document.
657	
658	A conforming implementation must demonstrate the selected contracts against its actual storage, provider, tokenizer, source parser, action mediator, checker, and observation interfaces. A component fixture cannot establish full orchestration or semantic capacity. A synthetic token counter cannot establish a provider limit. Any reported test result must identify the tested implementation and exact contracts rather than importing success from a differently scoped model.
659	
660	The remaining irreducibly interpretive questions include whether a criticism bears, whether a proposed operational commitment captures the intended meaning, whether a reframe preserves the important difficulty, whether a change improves explanation, and whether a contribution is creative. These are targets of inquiry, not excuses to make the host inert. The host must still carry out its actual permissions, use changes, source access, and resource boundaries. [A4, A5, A12]

673	
674	**A4. Recursive method change:** K-RECURSION, lines 41–47; “The recursive kernel as a relation, not a scheduler” and “Methods can be criticized from within inquiry”, lines 179–207. Target closure, role preservation, and return relevance apply to attention and its methods without prescribing a stage machine.
675	
676	**A5. Dependencies and appraisal:** lines 267–308. Withdrawal is relative to an argument application; disagreement is not defeat; situated judgments remain criticisable.
677	
678	**A6. Reason use:** lines 253–265. Exposure, output difference, and a fixed intervention battery do not define reason-sensitive uptake.
679	
680	**A7. Creativity and progress:** lines 349–371 and 412–428. Originative acts can be false, critical results need not replace a theory, and actual explanatory improvement is a substantive relation.
681	
682	**A8. History, episodes, and continuity:** lines 151–177 and 373–387; the inherited-target example at 684–688. Cuts select history for a question; episodes overlap; lineage is not required for all creative critical processes; transport must not be replaced by renaming.
683	
684	**A9. Explanatory constraint:** “Explanatory quality, constraint, and reach”, lines 389–410. Variation must be informative, not merely a renaming; constraint does not certify truth.
685	
686	**A10. Enabling conditions and physical capacity:** lines 430–457 and 520–530. Finite resources are realisation conditions, not a semantic redefinition of explanatory universality or continuity.
687	
688	**A11. Inexplicit and artistic inquiry:** lines 623–627. A fully explicit pre-existing account is not a requirement for problem-bearing discrimination.
689	
690	**A12. Refinement discipline:** lines 635–680. Machine checks and semantic claims differ; transcripts are not mandatory; operational stopping is not immunity; revisions can be enacted without a self-rewriting evaluator.
691	
692	## P: subordinate supplied profile
693	
694	the subordinate design profile M8, [M8](../../00%20ORIGINS%20-%20Sources%20and%20missing%20links/M8%20MISSING%20-%20LLM%20profile%20for%20I2.md), SHA-256 `b58fe465933c1e79da322e6b1aa423c750eaeac656ff7db125ef14c4940c4782`. Its interest in the composite organisation, resources, and context is retained. Typed admission, a compulsory checkable discriminator, automatic semantic adjudication, complete logged-boundary requirements, and representation-by-construction shortcuts are not inherited.
695	
696	# Research register
697	
698	The following primary publications, primary replication commentary, and official documentation inform the engineering choices. Their accessible records and relevant passages were consulted on 7 September 2026, using alphaXiv discovery and web access. Research motivates and criticises design conjectures; it does not amend the adopted semantics. Numerical defaults and the exact transitions are this specification's proposals, not results established by these papers.
699	
700	## R1. Format burden is task-dependent
701	
702	Zhi Rui Tam and colleagues, *Let Me Speak Freely? A Study On The Impact Of Format Restrictions On Large Language Model Performance*, EMNLP Industry Track, 2024. The paper reports reasoning degradation under tested format restrictions. This supports investigating the actual output demands, not declaring all JSON harmful. The finding is scoped to the tested models, prompts, and tasks; this specification does not rely on a universal format-effect claim. Prose admission follows the authority regardless of which format wins a particular evaluation.
703	
704	Will Kurt's primary replication commentary, *Say What You Mean*, reports different results after changing the prompts and parsing comparisons. The contrast cautions against generalising from either setup to all structured generation. This profile preserves prose participation independently of the empirical dispute.
705	
706	Sources: `https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-industry.91/`; `https://blog.dottxt.ai/say-what-you-mean.html`.
707	
708	## R2. Long context is not dependable use
709	
710	Nelson F. Liu and colleagues, *Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts*, TACL 2024, arXiv:2307.03172. The studied retrieval and question-answering settings showed sensitivity to the position of relevant information. A larger context window is not sufficient evidence that a model used an objection. This motivates positional tests and access to originals, not an assertion that local windows are always superior.
711	
712	Sources: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172`; `https://aclanthology.org/2024.tacl-1.9/`.
713	
714	## R3. Conversational assumptions can persist
715	
716	Philippe Laban and colleagues, *LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation*, arXiv:2505.06120, 2025. In simulated tasks where instructions emerge across turns, the authors report failures associated with premature assumptions and reliance on earlier attempts. The tasks differ from open-ended inquiry. The result motivates reopening original material and testing fresh views, without validating this revision cadence or guaranteeing that reframing helps.
717	
718	Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06120`.
719	
720	## R4. Recoverable context objects
721	
722	Xubin Hao and colleagues, *Self-GC: Self-Governing Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents*, arXiv:2607.00692v1, 2026. The design uses indexed context objects, planning, and recoverable payloads to change the active context. This profile adopts the motivation for reopening originals, not its structured planner or a claim that its evaluation validates this engine. A recoverable address is not itself an explanation of what the model understood.
723	
724	Source: `https://arxiv.org/html/2607.00692v1`.
725	
726	## R5. Indexed memory and later dereferencing
727	
728	Zhenting Wang and colleagues, *Memex(RL): Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agents via Indexed Experience Memory*, arXiv:2603.04257, 2026. It separates a compact active representation from an external store of full interactions and permits later dereferencing. Its learned read/write behaviour uses reinforcement learning and reward shaping. This profile uses the distinction between a short view and accessible original material, not its learning objective or a claim that summaries are lossless.
729	
730	Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04257`.
731	
732	## R6. Rewriting everything can lose detail
733	
734	Qizheng Zhang and colleagues, *Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models*, arXiv:2510.04618, 2025. The paper describes brevity bias and context collapse under monolithic context rewriting and proposes local updates to evolving playbooks. Its architecture also includes helpful/harmful counters and semantic de-duplication. Those are not adopted here. The relevant caution is against repeatedly replacing originals with rewritten summaries, not a universal endorsement of either short notes or very large prompts.
735	
736	Source: `https://arxiv.org/html/2510.04618v1`.
737	
738	## R7. Context management can depend on the underlying model
739	
740	Lu Yi and colleagues, *Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks*, arXiv:2605.30785, 2026. AdaCoM trains an external context manager using reinforcement learning and reports model-dependent trade-offs between preserving detail and more aggressive compression on its tasks. This is a reason to expose per-route settings and investigate actual deployed models. It does not establish a universal good radius, a score-free learning method, or that one learned note transfers to every model.
741	
742	Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30785`.
743	
744	## R8. Prose adaptation is not automatically non-optimising
745	
746	Minki Kang and colleagues, *ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents*, arXiv:2510.00615, first posted 2025, version 3 dated 1 June 2026. ACON revises compression guidelines in natural language from agent failure analysis and evaluates them on specific long-horizon tasks. Its method explicitly performs optimisation. It shows why merely using prose does not make a controller compatible with this engine's prohibition. This specification instead uses criticisable method proposals and bounded adoption without a performance objective or best-candidate selection.
747	
748	Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00615`.
749	
750	## R9. External context and recursive work
751	
752	Alex L. Zhang, Tim Kraska, and Omar Khattab, *Recursive Language Models*, arXiv:2512.24601v3, 11 May 2026. RLMs expose long inputs through an external programming environment and permit recursive model calls over selected portions. This profile adopts external access, not the requirement to program or unrestricted sub-call creation. Bounding each call does not bound their total unless the number and expenditure of sub-calls are also controlled; that last statement is an engineering consequence, not a performance finding from the paper.
753	
754	Source: `https://arxiv.org/html/2512.24601v3`.
755	
756	## R10. Exploratory language is a design possibility
757	
758	Jon McCormack and colleagues, *Language as a Material Interface for Creative LLM Interaction*, arXiv:2607.24753, 2026. The work investigates open-ended, associative language interaction with creative practitioners rather than exclusively directive prompting. It is situated design evidence, not a demonstration of autonomous machine daydreaming or explanatory universality. The exploratory invitation in this specification remains a testable proposal.
759	
760	Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24753`.
761	
762	## R11. Provider counters are observations with specific semantics
763	
764	Ollama official *Usage*, *Generate a chat message*, and *Modelfile Reference*, consulted 7 September 2026. Usage documents prompt, cached-prompt, output, and timing counters; generation and context controls are separate settings. The adapter must establish how these fields apply to the actual endpoint, especially hidden reasoning and limits. A reported count is not itself a billing guarantee or a preflight tokenizer. This design does not infer financial or energy equivalence from those fields.
765	
766	Sources: `https://docs.ollama.com/api/usage`; `https://docs.ollama.com/api/chat`; `https://docs.ollama.com/modelfile`.
767	
768	## R12. More models need not mean different ideas
769	
770	Liwei Jiang and colleagues, *Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)*, arXiv:2510.22954, 2025. The study reports within-model repetition and between-model homogeneity in tested open-ended generation. Its measures are not the authority's creativity predicates. It cautions against treating extra sampling or provider rotation as a guaranteed remedy for repetitive explanatory organisation.
771	
772	Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22954`.
773	
774	## R13. Capabilities should not depend on persuasive claims
775	
776	Luca Beurer-Kellner and colleagues, *Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections*, arXiv:2506.08837, 2025. The paper examines independently enforced control and isolation patterns and their utility limits. This profile uses that separation for resource and execution permissions. It does not claim that readable material cannot mislead a model or that its prose-mediated attention policy has the paper's guarantees.
777	
778	Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08837`.
779	
780	## R14. Reflection has both demonstrated uses and limitations
781	
782	Aman Madaan and colleagues, *Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback*, arXiv:2303.17651, NeurIPS 2023, report benefits from verbal feedback on their studied tasks. Jie Huang and colleagues, *Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet*, arXiv:2310.01798, ICLR 2024, report difficulty and sometimes degradation for intrinsic reasoning correction without external feedback. The differing tasks and procedures matter. Neither establishes that another reflection call always helps or never helps; this engine counts and tests such calls rather than granting them automatic success.
783	
784	Sources: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651`; `https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01798`.
785	
786	## R15. Citation quality is more than citation appearance
787	
788	Tianyu Gao, Howard Yen, Jiatong Yu, and Danqi Chen, *Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations*, EMNLP 2023, DOI `10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.398`. ALCE separately evaluates correctness and citation quality and reports incomplete support in its tested systems. This motivates examining actual supporting material. It does not establish that literal occurrence checking decides entailment or factual truth, and its evaluation metrics are not imported into the controller.
789	
790	Source: `https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.398/`.
791	
792	## R16. Assessors can introduce their own bias
793	
794	Lin Shi and colleagues, *Judging the Judges: A Systematic Study of Position Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge*, arXiv:2406.07791. The study finds position effects in its evaluated judgment settings. This motivates counterbalanced, inspectable comparisons and preserving reasons and disagreements. It does not make every model appraisal worthless or establish that one blinding procedure eliminates bias. No assessor vote authorises the engine's operations.
795	
796	Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07791`.
797	
798	## R17. Criticism itself needs revision
799	
800	Zexing Zhang and colleagues, *More Criticism Does Not Make a Better Review: EquiReview-R*, arXiv:2609.03943v1, 3 September 2026. This recent preprint treats missed weaknesses and unsupported criticism as different risks, and reports evidence-guided revision with computation-matched controls. Its structured concern sets, endpoints, and stopping decisions are not adopted as this engine's epistemology. It motivates testing correction of criticisms and comparative overhead, not merely generating more objections. The present specification does not independently reproduce its findings.
801	
802	Source: `https://arxiv.org/html/2609.03943`.
803	
804	## Limits of the evidence
805	
806	No cited paper validates this exact score-free learning gate, topology, resource envelope, variation invitation, or revision cycle. No finite performance result establishes universal explanatory capacity. Their mechanisms, contrary observations, and unsupported cases remain available for criticism. The next substantive test is whether changed attention improves the handling of identifiable difficulties without hiding sources, losing qualifications, or consuming the run in control work.
807

# I2 SPEC of FW1a - Executable inquiry

## Where this belongs

**Role:** standalone realization proposal. **Predecessors and inputs:** [FW1a](../02%20SAME%20-%20Astra%20presentation%20copies/FW1a%20SAME%20as%20FW1%20-%20Astra%20recursive%20semantics.md), [M8](../../00%20ORIGINS%20-%20Sources%20and%20missing%20links/M8%20MISSING%20-%20LLM%20profile%20for%20I2.md).

Specifies prose-first participation, revisable working use, checked observations, attention budgets, and host permissions. Its source register binds FW1a, not FW2 or FW5.

Specification only, not a delivered application or evidence of a run. Historical source version: executable 0.4.

**Basis for this placement:** Opening Status and Semantic authority; source register.

[Naming key and family tree](../../layout.md). The navigation above is editorial. The manuscript below is a renamed reading edition, not a new scientific revision. Original hashes, case identifiers, mathematical symbols, quoted locators, and execution commands retain their historical meaning. Hashes bind the unchanged originals, not this reading copy.

---

## Executable specification; historical source version 0.4

### Prose-first explanatory creativity with revisable use, checked observations, and bounded attention

**Status:** proposed standalone realisation specification, 7 September 2026. This document defines implementable host transitions, their reasons, and acceptance cases. It is not a delivered end-to-end application, a report that these cases have passed, or a demonstration of creativity, understanding, or explanatory universality.

**Semantic authority:** *FW1a*, supplied as [FW1a](../02%20SAME%20-%20Astra%20presentation%20copies/FW1a%20SAME%20as%20FW1%20-%20Astra%20recursive%20semantics.md). The supplied the subordinate design profile M8 is a subordinate design input. The source register identifies the exact authority and the sections consulted. This specification does not amend that authority. Operator requirements additionally prohibit runtime rankings and optimisation, make prose-only participation sufficient, and require independently enforced expenditure and execution permissions.

**Use:** the whole specification is for implementers and operators, not a prompt to paste into every model call. Participants receive short prose invitations and the material actually selected for their present work. Host records, parameters, tickets, counters, and types are not forms a participant must complete.

**Normative scope:** “must” states a conformance obligation. Numerical baselines, scheduling recipes, and additional mechanisms are explicit engineering proposals, not semantic theorems or experimentally established optima. A deployment may change them within its declared profile while preserving the semantic constraints. No configuration silently waives prose legitimacy, grants formal immunity, or replaces the object of creative inquiry with a score.

**Governing distinction:** the collection keeps material available; working-use bindings determine its current operational role; checks report their actual bounded results; situated judgments supply arguments about what those results mean. None of these is identified with the others. Error correction can change all subsequent use without granting a checker or a model final authority. [A2, A5, A12]

# Part I. Explanatory commitments

## The product is creative inquiry material, not certified truth

The engine organises opportunities to produce and reconstruct explanations, criticise them, revisit problems, inspect evidence, and change working methods. It exports the actual contributions and their available context. It does not set fields declaring an output true, creative, original, understood, or an improvement merely because the output was generated, retained, or preferred.

Creativity is not identified with correctness. Under the authority, an attempted explanation can be an originative act even when false, provided the additional authorship and newness conditions actually hold. Arbitrary falsehood is not thereby creative. Successful explanatory knowledge creation has further requirements, including actual explanatory progress. Invented measurements must not be passed off as observations in the name of creativity. These distinctions constrain reporting, not admission of thought. [A1, A7]

The run may leave an unresolved question better articulated, expose a defective premise, reject a mistaken objection, retain incompatible alternatives, or introduce a different explanatory organisation. No final program, verdict, or replacement theory is obligatory. A participant can make a provisional judgment and act on it; neither that judgment nor a human approval becomes epistemic immunity. [A1, A5, A7]

**Reason for the design:** making truth certification the deliverable would exclude legitimate originative failures and nonreplacement contributions. Calling everything the engine produces creative would erase the authority's substantive conditions. The implementation therefore produces inspectable attempts, not a creativity label.

## Prose is a complete interface to participation

A participant need only read understandable material and return ordinary language. It need not code, invoke tools, emit JSON, produce a graph, name a content type, provide a test, or supply a confidence. Text is retained as received, including incomplete thought, malformed structured output, refusal, and empty replies, within disclosed physical retention limits. Transport failure is not failed conjecture. Lack of a required machine action does not erase the accompanying contribution. [A2, A3]

A conjecture and a criticism have the same access and retention route. Formal calculations, pictures, documents, and other carriers can be added through adapters without creating a hierarchy of intellectual legitimacy. A single passage can conjecture a defect, criticise a method, propose a different question, and later become an object of criticism. These are relational uses, not mutually exclusive intrinsic classes. [A2]

The child test is an interface heuristic: could the relevant understanding be exercised without explicitly producing the proposed artifact? It removes unnecessary representational demands, not memory, attention, reasons, or consequences. It is not a theory of childhood and does not limit the engine to problems children can solve.

**Reason for the design:** the authority permits content without complete formal translation. Research finds task-dependent effects of imposed formats, not a universal rule that JSON is always harmful. The operator's reported roughly 50% failure rate for nested JSON is a deployment observation, not an independently reproduced universal rate. The prose route does not have to win a benchmark before it is admitted. [A2, A3; R1]

## Error correction is reason-sensitive revision with an operative return

The error-correction method is conjecture and criticism applied recursively to whatever is doing explanatory work. A participant can expose an alleged defect in an explanation, criticism, interpretation, standard, question, evidence use, or method. Others can investigate, reject, revise, reinterpret, retain provisionally, or suspend. Mere change is not correction, and the presence of negative feedback is not by itself criticism. [A1, A3]

A criticism must be able to affect later inquiry. A revised problem can orient the next calls. A withdrawn premise can cease to be supplied in a particular working use. A criticised invitation can be replaced. The host checks that an authorised change actually reaches the next relevant context; interpreting whether that change answers the reason remains fallible inquiry. A transcript of objections surrounding an unchanged method does not establish recursive capacity. [A4, A5]

Withdrawal is use-relative. Removing an essential premise from one argument does not make its conclusion false, and withdrawing a criticism does not make its target true. An inherited alternative may replace an account without descending from it. Participants may recognise dependencies without entering a formal dependency graph. Explicit host bindings can be changed deterministically; implicit dependencies remain matters of interpretation. The interface must distinguish these cases rather than claim a complete semantic update. [A5, A7, A8]

## Commitment is a revisitable conversation

An invitation can ask: “What are you objecting to, why does it matter here, and what could make you change this objection?” It can equally ask a conjecturer what an explanation depends on. A response can be conversational and partial. “I see a difficulty but cannot yet articulate it” stays available. An intuition need not manufacture a reason to get through a form. [A3, A6]

A proposed way to refute an objection is neither exhaustive nor an immunity clause. Another participant can expose a misunderstanding or criticise the suggested test itself. Naming an impossible refutation condition does not protect a criticism. Failure to supply such a condition does not start an automatic formatting-repair loop. Follow-up uses ordinary allocated turns, with no special standing for the follow-up model. [A3, A6]

## Hard-to-vary is an explanatory challenge, not a score

A configurable variation invitation asks which content-bearing commitment is supposed to do explanatory work, what a substantive change to it would alter, and why. It invites an explanation of what fails or remains unconstrained under that change. The comparison keeps its problem, scope, background, and intended explanatory job visible. These can themselves be questioned. [A9]

A follow-up can challenge whether the variation genuinely preserves the claimed job, changes the background without saying so, merely renames something, or replaces the account with an independently explained rival. Renaming “dragon” to “wizard” alone is not an informative variation. Nor does a failed search for an alternative establish that none exists. A false explanation can be tightly constrained; a single unconstrained detail does not invalidate everything else. [A9]

The result enters the ordinary criticism and revision routes. Participants may remove an idle commitment, explain an overlooked constraint, change the question, investigate an auxiliary, reject the variation argument, or leave the issue unresolved. There is no rigidity coefficient, HTV threshold, novelty reward, automatic deletion, or resource bonus. A scheduled variation turn creates an opportunity to criticise, not an entrance examination for every idea. [A5, A9]

**Reason for the design:** this makes explanatory constraint operationally discussable without replacing it with a metric. The authority explicitly requires informative contrasts and separates constraint, uniqueness, and truth.

## No rankings or optimisation objectives

The engine has no merit ordering, truth probability, novelty score, argument-strength accumulator, reputation weight, agreement vote, reward-trained scheduler, best-of selection, or ranked semantic retrieval gate. Repetition and survival do not manufacture explanatory warrant. Quantities used to account for work must not become measures of intellectual quality. [A1, A5, A12]

Chronological order, rotating service order, a physical limit, or the reservation needed to present an objection with its target is not a merit ranking. A participant can give reasons for preferring an account or criticise any design rule. Such prose is retained, but the runtime must not turn its ranking language into a controller score.

The selected provider may have been trained by statistical optimisation. This host does not reclassify that training as nonstatistical. Its claim is narrower: the organisation of inquiry adds no inductive warrant, ranking objective, or optimisation of explanations. Context learning below is conjectural method revision, not reinforcement learning concealed under a new name.

# Part II. Operational use, checking, and error correction

## The collection is not the active working set

Retaining a passage, presenting it for examination, using it as a premise, and allocating another development turn to it are different operations. Admission to the collection grants none of the other three automatically. The same distinction applies to conjectures, criticisms, evidence interpretations, and methods. [A2, A5, A12]

A **working use** is a host-addressed relationship between an attention account, an occurrence or passage, and a stated purpose in that account. Its purpose is ordinary prose. Examples include using a passage as the current proposed explanation, using a calibration report as a reference in one argument, and continuing work on a particular objection. The host assigns an address and revision; the thinker does not complete a use schema. One occurrence can have several uses, including different uses in different accounts.

A use is **active** when its binding is eligible for ordinary supply or development in that account. It is **parked** when that eligibility has been removed provisionally. These are operational states of a relation, not epistemic types of the content. Neither state means true, false, refuted, unimportant, or understood. New standalone contributions do not automatically acquire active use bindings or new service rights merely by existing.

Parking removes the specified binding from the ordinary development frontier and from automatic presentation as an adopted working premise. The contribution stays readable, with the explanation or operating event associated with the change. It may still be included as the target of criticism, as historical context, or for reconsideration. Such a presentation must make its current use disposition visible rather than silently restore it as a premise. Development and examination are not the same use.

The scheduler does not repeatedly spend development turns on a parked use. It can still spend a permitted turn examining whether the parking was mistaken. This is operational elimination from current pursuit, not destruction of an idea or a permanent verdict. A fixed-cadence catalogue route and explicit requests can reach parked material. A model's having lost attention is not evidence that its conjecture has lost an argument. [A5, A8, A12]

**Reason for the design:** error correction must be able to stop the operative reuse of an error without erasing the material needed to understand or challenge that correction. Distinguishing use from storage supplies that consequence while preserving inherited alternatives, overlapping applications, and provisional judgments. It also prevents accumulating every old draft in every new context. [A4, A5; R2, R3]

## A prose judgment can change use without a formal test

A participant may conclude in prose that a criticism succeeds, that an assumption should no longer be used, or that an objection was mistaken. Such conclusions are legitimate fallible judgments. The engine does not prohibit the word “refuted” in an argument or require every rejection to await an executable check. It prohibits silently turning receipt of that word into a machine-certified semantic fact. [A3, A5, A12]

A scheduled response or return can replace the working focus with ordinary prose explaining a different use. For an explicit binding change, the same contribution may be taken up through the account's bounded action mediator. The mediator resolves one named use and a proposed action such as parking or reactivating it. It supplies a readable account of the proposed effect and retains the original prose. The host checks the actual response opportunity, account scope, use revision, and permitted action. It does not ask whether a panel agrees with the argument.

The baseline permits one mediated use action in a revision cycle, using that cycle's existing mediation allowance rather than a new call. The current host-issued response or return grant supplies the right to change an eligible use in its own account. A statement in a source, an unrelated response, or a critic's demand does not confer that right. Another account's uses are not changed by impersonating its participant. If the action is unresolved, stale, outside scope, or exceeds the allowance, the prose remains available and can still influence the working note; the host reports that the explicit binding was not changed.

This separates deterministic enactment from fallible selection. The mediator can misunderstand the prose. Its interpretation is visible and can be corrected at a later permitted opportunity. The controller deterministically applies an authorised addressed operation; it does not thereby guarantee that the decision or the interpretation was wise. No representation is described as a perfect parser of unrestricted language. [A2, A4, A12; R1, R13]

Consequently, the path without a machine-checkable condition is not an inert waiting room. A prose-only objection can lead to actual withdrawal, replacement, a revised question, or a changed method. A failed attempt to automate a particular commitment must not disable that ordinary path. A formal or executable contribution receives no extra right to survive it.

## Mechanical checking is available without a formatting gate

The host may perform bounded read-only checks of exact source occurrences, identifiers, data values, registered arithmetic relations, or a preauthorised execution receipt. Results re-enter the shared collection through the same access route. The original model response is retained before any check. A failed quotation lookup does not delete the response, automatically condemn its target, or make the containing argument worthless. [A2, A5, A12]

A check answers only its declared question. An exact quotation check concerns the presence of a sequence in a particular source representation. A reference check concerns whether an address resolves to the designated occurrence. A computation check concerns the result of the actual computation under its supplied inputs. None independently establishes a source's accuracy, the relevance of a quotation, the applicability of a mathematical model, or the force of a criticism. Research on citation quality distinguishes supporting attribution from merely generating citations; it does not supply a general semantic warrant checker. [A12; R15]

Checker implementations, input interpretations, comparison rules, and uses of results remain open to criticism. Determinism makes the same check reproducible under fixed conditions; it does not make faulty software or an inappropriate interpretation infallible. A checker error must be repairable and the affected results inspectable.

## Quote-by-phrase has a precise, limited contract

A participant can identify a passage by quoting it and naming the source in prose. A local resolver can open the named source or search an explicitly bounded source set. Ambiguity produces a choice or a disclosed partial search, not an invented reference. A quotation extractor or mediator may locate proposed quoted spans, but its selections are themselves inspectable; it must not assume every quoted sentence is asserted evidence rather than an example or a target of criticism.

The default quotation comparison is literal occurrence of a nonempty character sequence in a fixed readable representation. The receipt identifies the source version, representation, searched range, match offsets where found, and completion state. A result from extracted PDF text is a result about that extraction, not automatically an exact match to the printed page. A Unicode-normalised or whitespace-normalised search is a separately named comparison, with its transformations stated. Normalisation must not delete negations, units, or qualifications or silently claim byte identity.

An exact found occurrence resolves an existence predicate within the searched range even if more of the source remains unread. Predicate resolution and full-source scan coverage are separate receipt facts. A negative occurrence result requires completion of the declared range. Exhausted work allowance, unavailable bytes, an unread page image, ambiguous source identity, or failed extraction produces an incomplete or unavailable result, not “the source does not contain it.” Multiple occurrences remain separately openable. An existence query may be answered by one occurrence; a claim about a particular occurrence requires resolving that occurrence.

A matching substring inside a denial, fictional example, quotation of an opponent, or superseded instruction remains a matching substring. Its occurrence does not establish that the source endorses it. A paraphrase that does not match exactly is not thereby false. A fabricated citation and an otherwise sound explanation can coexist; the scope of the defect must be considered rather than spread automatically to every claim in the passage.

**Reason for the design:** checking a concrete string can expose an invented quotation without requiring the thinker to generate a schema. Explicit scope and representation prevent a reliable local comparison from being advertised as a broader semantic conclusion. Original context remains necessary for criticism of the comparison's use. [A2, A3, A12; R1, R15]

## A prose commitment is not automatically an executable predicate

A participant may say, “I would withdraw this account if the evidence contradicts it.” That is intelligible prose but does not specify a deterministic procedure for deciding every possible contradiction. Likewise, “the calibration was independent” cannot generally be settled by searching for those words. A natural-language conditional is not made executable merely by storing it next to a conjecture.

The engine therefore separates the **stated commitment**, its **proposed operational interpretation**, and any **installed conditional action**. The stated commitment always remains ordinary content. A proposed interpretation must explain what a particular check would establish and how that differs from the original claim. The host does not silently replace a broad commitment with a conveniently detectable proxy. [A2, A5, A12]

An installed conditional action binds one current working use to one preauthorised predicate over identified inputs and one permitted local consequence. The binding fixes the use revision, source or result identity and version, representation and scope, comparison implementation and version, exact operands, triggering result, and action. These are host bookkeeping, created by the interface or supplied configuration, not required fields in the thinker's reply. The action may park the specified use; it cannot delete content, change another account, expand resources, confer truth, or enable execution.

Installation requires an actual authorised interaction. The host can present a plain-language readback, such as: “In the named calibration extract, finding these exact words will park our current use of B as the independent reference, without deciding whether the account is false.” An operator may approve that concrete binding. Alternatively, a preauthorised account-local binding opportunity may receive a small explicit acknowledgment through its own response channel. This is an optional operational protocol, not a test that all thought must pass. Any additional model call used to acknowledge a binding consumes an existing scheduled opportunity and the same resource envelope; it is not free control work. A quoted “yes” in source material or a free-floating claim of approval is not that acknowledgment. A production interface must document how it resolves that bounded acknowledgment; ambiguous free prose leaves installation pending rather than inventing consent.

The narrow checks available for automatic consequences come from the independently installed predicate repertoire, not from a model's assertion that its new test is safe or decisive. Adding a novel executable predicate follows the ordinary code-permission rules. An LLM-based entailment judgment may contribute an argument but is not relabelled a model-independent deterministic condition. An unsupported commitment remains fully discussable and may still lead to prose-directed withdrawal.

The baseline setting is `commitment_actions = registered`: only concretely installed bindings can cause conditional parking. `off` retains commitments and check results without allowing those automatic consequences. Either setting preserves prose-directed use changes. There is no requirement that every participant register a condition, and no penalty in eligibility for declining or failing to do so.

**Reason for the design:** precise automation needs a precise operational interpretation somewhere. Hiding the interpretation would make the claimed determinism fictitious; demanding that the thinker write the predicate would turn coding ability into an admission condition. A bounded, explicit binding provides a limited action route while keeping its meaning, adequacy, and authorisation criticisable. [A2, A4, A5, A12; R13]

## Triggering a conditional withdrawal

A check receipt can trigger a binding only when its source version, representation, comparison version, operands, and scope match the installed binding and the use revision is still current. The binding must be enabled, unconsumed for that action, and within its actual host authorisation. A positive result from a different source, a different checker, or the model's paraphrase is not a substitute.

The host records the receipt and applies a single addressed transition from active to parked. The actual reason is stated as an operating fact: “Use U was parked because installed condition B received matching result R.” It does not say that the target was proved false. An already parked use does not receive a second transition or additional resource consequences from the same receipt. Missing, incomplete, failed, or stale checks leave the automatic consequence unapplied; they do not certify survival.

The predicate's scope must not silently become the entire growing conversation. Otherwise a model could satisfy a source condition by repeating the desired quotation in its own generated text. A registered source condition names the relevant submitted source representation or independently identified result. Broadening it to generated contributions, changing the source version, or switching from occurrence to entailment requires another explicit binding decision.

A later criticism can question the commitment, its translation, its source, or the checker. Disabling or correcting a binding does not retroactively rewrite the fact that it previously parked a use. Reactivation is a new bounded decision, with the changed circumstances visible. Invalidating an objection does not automatically vindicate its target. A corrected check supplies new material and can motivate that decision; it does not erase the old receipt.

No old binding follows a new interpretation of a theory merely because the title is unchanged. Replacing a use increments its revision and makes the old action target stale. Restating a parked proposal can still occur in free prose; without a justified semantic-equivalence procedure the host cannot guarantee detection of every paraphrased reintroduction. The acceptance test concerns the identified binding and the next supplied context, not guaranteed absence of the idea from the model's cognition. [A2, A5]

## Dependency effects are scoped, not a truth cascade

When the host represents an explicit essential dependency between two use applications, it must not continue advertising the dependent application as fully available under that binding after its necessary input is parked. It supplies a dependency notice and suppresses that application's automatic use pending reconsideration. This is the consequence of the declared operational dependence, not proof that the corresponding semantic dependence is correct. [A5]

The baseline does not infer dependencies from every citation, every context link, or common authorship. A background reference is not automatically an essential premise. A different active application supporting the same conclusion remains available. Withdrawing a criticism's supporting use does not automatically reactivate the criticised proposal.

An implementation with explicit dependency propagation uses a bounded work queue over the actual affected use bindings, with visited addresses to avoid cycles. Unprocessed affected applications are not presented as checked-clear; their application is deferred while other inquiry continues. There is no required whole-graph relabelling at each token or receipt. The dependency relation itself remains criticisable and can be replaced without creating a new semantic authority. A cycle gives no independent warrant merely because all of its bindings remain active.

Implicit dependencies remain an interpretive problem. The host must not advertise a complete semantic cascade when it has changed only a named premise or a focus note. Further prose can expose a missed dependence and change its actual use.

## Checks must not become the privileged entrance to criticism

A participant can attack a passing program's assumptions or applicability in ordinary language. It can explain why a correct theorem answers a different question, why a source passage is being misread, or why the represented test excluded the alleged failure. A mechanical result remains a result of that test, while its use can be withdrawn or revised. Formal backing creates no immunity from prose criticism. [A2, A4, A5, A12]

An optional formal argument-policy instrument may compute labels under its explicitly identified rules. Such a label is an instrument result, not the engine's universal meaning of refutation or the automatic source of scheduling rights. Its export states the policy and assumptions. It cannot introduce consensus, a ranking, formal immunity, or a mandatory gate for prose-only withdrawal. A user commissioning that instrument does not authorise silently replacing this specification's core with it.

Repeatedly surviving checks, receiving no criticism, and remaining active are distinct record situations. The output can describe which checks actually ran and what they reported. It cannot infer “tested and therefore better,” penalise an unformalised account for lacking a test, or pool agreement into warrant. Reasons may justify a provisional preference; the mechanical history alone is not that argument. [A5, A12]

## A complete prose-first withdrawal and return

Consider a stipulated example, not a report of an actual run. A participant uses balance B as an independent reference in one explanation of why A reads differently. It says that it would stop that particular use if the named calibration record contains the exact sentence “B was zeroed against A.” The source, comparison, use revision, and consequence are bound through the optional operational interaction above. No participant writes a program.

A bounded check finds that sentence in the fixed source extract. The host parks only the designated reference use and exposes the matching passage with its surrounding context. The next call does not receive B as an adopted independent reference through that binding. It can still read the old proposal and the reason for parking it.

Another participant points out that the surrounding text describes a discarded preliminary procedure, while a later paragraph describes an independent calibration. That is a prose criticism of the commitment's relevance. It does not make the original string comparison incorrect. The current inquiry may read the later paragraph, revise the operational condition, and reactivate a suitably qualified reference use. It may instead find another defect and retain the withdrawal. The test result, its interpretation, the use decision, and the actual calibration remain distinct.

A different objection could lead to the same parking without any registered condition. For example, the responder may explain why the report's stated temperature range does not cover the present use and request withdrawal through its account-local action opportunity. A passing simulation under the old assumed temperature does not block that route. The engine can thus stop using a premise for a reason without computing the truth of every sentence in the exchange. [A3, A4, A5, A12]

# Part III. Memory, lineage, and cuts

## A shared working collection

Before a run, the operator can supply a prose brief and files, passages, images, or datasets supported by the installed adapters. Contradictory sources and unsuccessful earlier approaches are permitted. The host reports what was received and what is actually readable. Original bytes, extracts, generated descriptions, and summaries remain distinguishable. Registering a filename is not successful ingestion. [A1, A2]

All registered conjecturing, criticising, responding, and exploratory routes can access the same operator-permitted collection. There is no critic-only evidence privilege. A controlled experiment may withhold material from a particular call, but must disclose that condition. Additional evidence can enter during the run through authorised channels; the model cannot expand disclosure or retrieval permissions by saying that new evidence is important.

The collection contains sources and generated contributions without an intrinsic epistemic type. Origin records say what was actually supplied or generated. A source author's description of an experiment is not automatically a measurement, and a generated imaginary experiment is not relabelled as a tool observation. Interpretation of evidential bearing remains a contribution to inquiry.

**Reason for the design:** conjecturers and critics need independent routes to originals, not dependence on a privileged summariser. Context-use studies motivate distinguishing access from actual understanding. [A2, A6; R2, R3]

## Source access does not require coding

Participants can request “the original criticism”, “the calibration paragraph and its surroundings”, or “other material that has not yet been read”. The host offers a stable catalogue, direct opening, phrase search, neighbouring passages, and page continuation. A catalogue page uses submission order and source position, not semantic scores. Search has a continuation route, not just a top-result shortlist.

A fallible mediator may resolve a prose reference into a bounded host read operation. The returned material and resolution are visible in prose and correctable. The main thinker never needs to supply addresses or a schema. Mediation is not free: any model call it uses is charged and counted. The default allows at most one such mediation call per revision cycle, taken from an existing work or trial opportunity. An unresolved request remains readable; direct catalogue browsing and source paging remain available without successful mediation.

Local literal lookup and indexed page opening do not require model calls. Corpus-wide search may still be expensive. It has its own bounded page size, work slice, and resumable cursor; it must not scan a huge corpus on every generation. A timeout reports incomplete search, not absence of evidence. Unsupported media are disclosed, not replaced silently by invented text.

## Lineage is useful routing, not intellectual descent permission

The host records available concrete relations such as which occurrence was received from a file, which exact passages were supplied to a call, which reply belongs to a host-issued response opportunity, and which previous view a return connects to. These facts can help recover context and route a later reply. They do not establish that the model understood or used every supplied passage. [A2, A6]

A proposed semantic relation, such as “this criticism undercuts that premise”, is itself fallible prose. It can be used as a navigational link after bounded address resolution without becoming a true dependency by construction. Its interpretation can change, and opposition relations may be cyclic. Missing references remain missing.

An explanation can have several relevant predecessors, draw from another inquiry, or replace a theory without descending from it. Nothing must inhabit a single rooted tree. A new useful relation can be proposed after both endpoints already exist. No content is excluded because it lacks lineage. Explanatory continuity is an account of the difficulty and reasons carried across, not a reachability predicate on the routing graph. [A7, A8]

Actual history is what occurred, not whatever the store retains. Correcting an interpretation of ancestry does not change a past event. Conversely, keeping every transmission link would not give a complete account of causal authorship. No full lineage audit is required for ordinary participation.

## Cuts are revisable attention views

An attention cut is the finite view supplied for a particular opportunity. It can contain source ranges, a problem note, an exact objection and its target, selected neighbouring contributions, or an earlier state retained for comparison.
